---
title: "The two runs, explained"
subtitle: "What each command did, and why the test run and the final run look so alike"
---


::: {.cell}

:::


::: {.in-short}
**In short.** You ran the same study twice, plus the extra Sámi test. The **test run** (`batch-pilot`) only searched.
The **final run** (`final`) searched in exactly the same way **and** asked an AI to write an
answer for every search. The searches gave
**identical results** in both
runs. Then you made blank checking sheets for two people and ran the scoring. The scores are
empty because nobody has filled in the sheets yet. That is expected.
:::

## The four commands


::: {.cell layout-align="left"}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|          Step           |                        Command                        |                                                                             What it does                                                                             |        Cost         |                    Status                    |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|----------------------------------------------|
|       1. Test run       |   `run_study_batch.R ... results/batch-pilot none`    |                                           Searches Finna in the three ways for all questions. **No AI.** A safe test run.                                            |        Free         |                     Done                     |
|      2. Final run       |  `run_study_batch.R ... results/final openai --demo`  |                        The same searches, **plus** an AI answer for each search (3 per question). Also copies the results into the demo app.                         | A small OpenAI bill |                     Done                     |
| 3. Make checking sheets |         `annotation.R sheets results/final 2`         |                    Makes blank spreadsheets for **two people** to judge the records and the AI's sentences, with the source of each item hidden.                     |        Free         | Done (157 records, 468 sentences per person) |
|   4. Score the sheets   |          `annotation.R score results/final`           |                                              Reads the **filled-in** spreadsheets and calculates scores and agreement.                                               |        Free         |    Ran too early: sheets are still empty     |
|  5. Sámi test (extra)   | `run_sami_sensitivity.R ... results/sami-sensitivity` |Runs all questions twice, back to back: search C with Finnish, Swedish and English thesaurus names, then with Northern Sámi names added. **No AI.** See [Extra tests](extra-tests.qmd).|        Free         |            Done (30 October 2026)            |


:::
:::


## Test run and final run: what is the same, what is different

| | Test run (`batch-pilot`) | Final run (`final`) |
|---|---|---|
| When | 30 October 2026, 00:25 | 30 October 2026, 00:44 |
| Questions | 13 | 13 |
| Searches (3 per question) | 39 | 39 |
| AI answers | None | Yes, by openai |
| Sentences to check | None | 468 |
| Copied into the demo app | No | Yes (`--demo`) |
| heritageRAG version | 0.3.0 | 0.3.0 |
| annif package version | 0.1.1 | 0.1.1 |
| Annif model | `yso-en` (backend *nn_ensemble*, model last changed 2025-09-16); `yso-fi` (backend *nn_ensemble*, model last changed 2025-09-16) | `yso-en` (backend *nn_ensemble*, model last changed 2025-09-16); `yso-fi` (backend *nn_ensemble*, model last changed 2025-09-16) |

**The searches were exactly the same.**
For all 39 searches, the number of matching records, the records kept, the number
of institutions and the number of languages are
identical between the two runs, which were
19 minutes apart.

This tells us two useful things:

1. **The search part is repeatable.** Run twice with the same settings, it gives the same
   evidence. (Finna's collections do change slowly over weeks and months, which is why every
   run records its date.)
2. **The final run is the one to report.** It contains everything the test run has, plus the
   AI answers. Keep the test run as proof that the searches are stable.

## Why the scores are empty

The `score` command reads the spreadsheets that the two checkers fill in. You ran it straight
after making the blank sheets, so it found 0
judgements and every score came out empty (shown as "NA" in the files). Nothing is wrong:
run it again once both people have finished. The [Human checking](human-check.qmd) page
explains what they need to do. When the sheets are filled, that page shows the results
automatically.

## What is in each folder

### At the top of `results/final`

| File | What it contains |
|---|---|
| `batch_metrics.csv` | One row per search: how many words were used, how many records matched in Finna, how many were kept, how many institutions and languages |
| `batch_queries.csv` | The exact search sent to Finna for each question and search type |
| `batch_overlap.csv` | How many records two searches have in common |
| `batch_annif_mapping.csv` | Every subject word Annif suggested and what we did with it |
| `batch_visibility_shift.csv` | How much the mix of institutions, languages, material types, decades and subjects changed between searches |
| `batch_temporal.csv` | The years covered by each search |
| `batch_themes.csv` | The most common subject words in each search |
| `batch_traceability.csv` | For each AI answer: how many sentences cite records, and where those records came from |
| `batch_summary_*.csv` | The same, averaged over all questions |
| `run_info.csv`, `sessionInfo.txt` | When the run happened and which software versions were used (from heritageRAG 0.3.0 also the label languages and the Annif model) |
| `annif_models.csv`, `batch_annif_models.csv` | Which Annif model answered: project, backend and model date (from heritageRAG 0.3.0) |
| `batch_anchors.csv`, `batch_diagnostics.csv` | How each key word was matched in the thesaurus, and every message from the tool (from heritageRAG 0.3.0) |
| `failures.csv` | Questions that crashed (none in this run) |
| `paper/` | Ready-made figures and tables for the paper |
| `annotation/` | The checking sheets, the secret keys (`KEY_*`) and the scores |

### Inside each question's folder (for example `results/final/women-advertising/`)

| File | What it contains |
|---|---|
| `query_plan.csv` | The three searches and how many records each matched |
| `facet_terms.csv` | Every search word and where it came from (you, Annif or the thesaurus) |
| `annif_concepts.csv`, `anchor_concepts.csv` | Annif's suggestions; the thesaurus concept found for each of your words |
| `annif_model.csv`, `diagnostics.csv` | The Annif model that answered, and the tool's messages for this question (from heritageRAG 0.3.0) |
| `concept_labels.csv`, `concept_relations.csv` | Official names in three languages; related, wider and narrower concepts |
| `retrieved_records.csv` | Every record kept, with the word that matched it |
| `query_record_provenance.csv` | Which search found which record, in what position |
| `metrics.csv`, `overlap.csv`, `visibility_*.csv`, `temporal_coverage.csv`, `themes.csv` | The comparisons for this one question |
| `narratives.md` | The three AI answers, readable as text |
| `claims.csv`, `traceability.csv` | The AI answers split into sentences, and their citations |
| `study.rds` | Everything above in one R file |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Updating this report after a new run

Copy the new results into the report and render it again:

```bash
Rscript prepare_data.R ../heritageRAG/results/final ../heritageRAG/results/batch-pilot ../heritageRAG/results/sami-sensitivity
quarto render
```

The third folder (the Sámi test on [Extra tests](extra-tests.qmd)) is optional. To redo the
analysis and the [paper figures](paper-figures.qmd) with a newer heritageRAG without searching
again, first run `Rscript scripts/refresh_analysis.R results/final` in the heritageRAG folder. Every number
and chart on these pages is recalculated from the files. Only the short notes in `notes.csv`
are written by hand, so check those after a new run.
:::
